text: This is Halden. Rivers bend, rails curve, and nothing lines up.
So the map tells a useful lie. It throws away distance, and keeps the connections.
Rule one. Horizontal, vertical, or forty-five degrees. Nothing else.
Rule two. One line, one colour, one weight.
Rule three. A tick is a stop. A ring is a change.
Zones tell you what it costs.
You are here, at Quill Lane. The lantern festival is at Rook Point.
Round the Ring, change at Ember Wharf.
A map doesn't show the city. It shows you the way.
